claims.text: Antifungal shampoo (eg, ketoconazole 2% or 1%) at least twice a week; because it tends to be chronic and often recurs, long-term use once or twice weekly is often required.
claims.quote: Treatment of seborrheic dermatitis of the scalp should include shampooing at least twice a week, because less frequent shampooing enables proliferation of Malassezia. Antifungal shampoos (eg, ketoconazole 2% or 1%) are highly effective in controlling the dandruff of seborrheic dermatitis (1). Because seborrheic dermatitis tends to be chronic and often recurs with cessation of treatment, long-term use of antifungal shampoos (eg, once or twice weekly) is often required.

claims.text: Face and folds, milder cases: ketoconazole 2% cream or another imidazole twice daily is often sufficient.
claims.quote: For seborrheic dermatitis in nonterminal hair-bearing areas (eg, nasolabial folds, postauricular areas, sternum), treatment is similar. However, creams (which are typically not acceptable in hair-bearing areas) are preferred to solutions. For milder cases, 2% ketoconazole cream or other topical imidazoles applied twice daily are often sufficient.

claims.text: Infants, severe cases: ketoconazole 2% or econazole 1% cream
claims.quote: Topical antifungals such as ketoconazole 2% cream or econazole 1% cream can also be helpful in severe cases.

claims.text: Effective for treatment and maintenance on the face and scalp (SORT A)
claims.quote: Topical antifungal agents are effective in treatment and maintenance of seborrheic dermatitis of the face and scalp.11,13 | | A
